newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines says raw sugar production to fall.
newsitem.headline: Philippines says raw sugar production to fall.

text.p: The Philippines Sugar Regulatory Administration (SRA) said on Tuesday that raw sugar output in the 1996-97 crop year ending August would fall to 1.8 million tonnes from a previously forecast 1.9 million tonnes.
SRA administrator Wilson Gamboa also told reporters that he expected the present sugar glut in the country to be mopped up by August this year.
He also said that sugar production in 1997-98 was likely to be 1.7 million tonnes, a shortfall of 487,000 tonnes.
"We are in fact revising our 1996-97 target due to typhoon damage in western Visayas island last year," Gamboa said.
Western Visayas accounts for 54 percent of the country's land planted to sugar.

"The typohons damaged between 20 and 25 percent of total sugar land in western Visayas," Gamboa said. He said he expected total sugar available in 1996-97 at 2.528 million tonnes, including 686,000 tonnes in stock at the beginning of the crop year and the minimum 43,000 tonnes which has to be imported under World Trade Organisation laws.
Consumption in 1996-97 is forecast at 2.15 million tonnes, including 250,000 tonnes contracted exports to the United States.
In 1997-98, Gamboa said output would fall as farmers switched to other crops because of the current glut.
